correctness.rationale: Let d>=2,m=d+1 and a unit-edge regular d-simplex, X uniform interior, and D(X)=min_i ||X-v_i||. In barycentric coordinates lambda, the exact identity ||X-v_i||²=(1+sum lambda_j²)/2-lambda_i yields Delta=R²-D²=T-H/2 with R²=d/(2m), T=max_i(lambda_i-1/m), H=sum_i(lambda_i-1/m)². The inequality H<=T proves unique farthest nearest-vertex distance at the centroid. For 0<t<=t0=1/[m(m-1)], {T<=t} is a homothetic simplex of normalized volume (mt)^d. Disintegrate by outer facet: conditional Dirichlet_d(1,...,1) direction P independent of radial T, with H=Q T² where Q=m² sum P_j²-m positive in [m/(m-1),m(m-1)]. For epsilon<t0/2, the inequality Delta>=T/2 excludes all outer cells and T->T-Q T²/2 is strictly increasing, so the positive root gives the exact Dirichlet expectation. Lagrange inversion gives absolutely convergent positive moments and explicitly E Q=m, E Q²=m²(m²+7m-6)/[(m+1)(m+2)], hence the stated eps and eps² coefficients. Independent Fraction arithmetic recomputed moments for d=2..14. The iid maximum law e^(-x^d) follows from leading (m epsilon)^d tail. Scope only fixed d and small endpoint window; finite checks not an all-d proof.
